newsitem.title: USA: Countrywide Credit second quarter earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: Countrywide Credit second quarter earnings rise.

text.p: Countrywide Credit Industries Inc., the nation's largest independent residential mortgage lender and servicer, said its earnings for the second quarter rose 28 percent despite higher interest rates.
Earnings for the fiscal quarter ended Aug. 31 were $62.5 million, or 60 cents a share, compared with $49 million, or 49 cents a share the year before.
Revenues for the Pasadena, Calif.-based company rose to $271 million from $209 million.
"This performance is particularly notable because our earnings continued to increase despite rising and generally higher interest rates," said David Loeb, chairman of Countrywide.

The company's loan production for the quarter was $9.2 billion compared to $8.9 billion in the year-ago quarter. Purchase mortgage activity was $7.1 billion in this year's second quarter and $6.3 billion in last year's second quarter.
Refinancing activity decreased, due to an increase in interest rates, the company said. Quarterly prepayments also declined in response to higher rates, it said.
Countrywide Credit stock was unchanged at $24.125 in afternoon trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
